strengths: Strong and consistent empirical improvements across multiple benchmarks and models (22-43% gains), particularly effective for smaller/less capable models
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablations, online graph construction scenarios, and testing across diverse benchmark characteristics
Well-motivated problem formulation with intuitive episodic/procedural memory analogy; clear presentation through figures and running examples
Practical design: no fine-tuning required; adaptive summarization tool allows flexible on-demand state consolidation
Thorough ablation studies examining component contributions, weight design variants, and graph-leveraging strategies
weaknesses: Critical underspecification of the summarization mechanism: decision criteria for invoking summarization are not algorithmic; state summary content and similarity computation metric are completely undefined, severely compromising reproducibility

Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing ideas (episodic memory + procedural memory + tool graphs) without deep novel mechanisms; core contribution is relatively straightforward integration
Baseline comparison concerns: ToolNet re-implemented from scratch without validation against original; unclear how implementation differences may bias results; re-implementation details missing

Insufficient design justification: weight formula (Eq. 1) parameter c never discussed or ablated; efficiency term (reciprocal of nij) lacks principled justification; no sensitivity analyses on key hyperparameters
Missing computational cost analysis: no reporting of summarization tool invocation frequency, computational overhead, or efficiency comparisons despite adding new inference steps

Limited error analysis and generalization: no qualitative case studies of successes/failures; all experiments restricted to OpenAI models; no sensitivity to training set size; statistical significance not reported (no error bars/confidence intervals)

Technical clarity issues: state information storage on edges depends on training-time summarization decisions (fragile); similarity metric for state matching completely unspecified; state-summary-only ablation (Table 4) questions whether graph structure is the key driver

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of limitations in existing episodic and tool-only approaches; compelling example (Figure 1)
Clean and intuitive State-Integrated Tool Graph design that elegantly combines episodic and procedural memory in unified structure
Grounded in cognitive science (episodic vs. procedural memory) providing strong conceptual foundation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse benchmarks with multiple base models showing consistent 7.9%-43.0% improvements; particularly strong gains on weaker models
Thorough ablation studies (Table 4) systematically validating component contributions and design choices
Clear and well-structured presentation with excellent figures effectively communicating methodology
Practical consideration of scenarios without training data (Section 5.3)
weaknesses: Insufficient technical details harm reproducibility: state summarization tool design vague (when/how to invoke?), no example summaries provided, parameter c in Eq. 1 not discussed, generation mechanism unclear
Computational overhead not quantified despite LLM-based summarization costs; claim of 'reducing computation' (contribution 2) unvalidated; no inference time or latency comparison
Baseline fairness concerns: ToolNet re-implemented due to missing code (risk of suboptimal implementation), some baselines show negative improvements suggesting implementation/tuning issues
Limited behavioral analysis: no error analysis, failure cases, or investigation of when state vs. weight guidance is most beneficial
Weight design (Eq. 1) appears ad-hoc; no justification for specific formulation combining success count and efficiency; missing sensitivity analysis for parameter c
Scalability concerns underexplored: data requirements unclear, behavior with rare tool combinations not discussed, evaluation limited to dialogue-based telecom/retail domains
No statistical rigor: missing confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests despite LLM stochasticity
Incremental novelty: combines existing techniques (tool graphs, state summarization, retrieval) without fundamentally new algorithmic insights
Missing implementation details prevent full reproducibility: state summary prompts, hyperparameter selection guidance, no code release mentioned
